source: Recovered from Archive::Open 0x38e40 and its header reader 0x397b0, which is the code the game itself runs.

header_2048.read: ReadFile of exactly 0x800 bytes; the reader rejects anything else, which is why an archive must be at least 2048 bytes
header_2048.off 0x00: the ASCII string "ARC" (compared against the constant at 0x308454)
header_2048.off 0x18: u32 file offset of the block table = 462022506

tables.block_table: at 0x18, blockCount entries of 12 bytes each, each entry {u32 offset, u32 storedLength, u32 field3}
tables.name_table: immediately after the block table, nameLength bytes of consecutive NUL-terminated ASCII names, one per file
tables.verification: every consecutive pair satisfies offset + storedLength == next.offset, with 0 exceptions across all 5264 transitions, so the block table is a contiguous, correctly understood layout

block_header.layout: u16 length, 3-byte magic (MSH/ANM/TEX), u8 version, u32 zero, u32 field1, u32 field2, then payload
block_header.observed: block 0 at 2048 is MSH version 3 with field1=38 and field2=34
block_header.payload: starts near offset 56 but the bytes are not plaintext and are not zlib or raw deflate

not_solved.compression: no zlib or raw-deflate stream exists anywhere in block 0, so the payload uses a different scheme or none
not_solved.strings: the region that looks like "Creatures\\Anomali" continues with 0A 00 F0 02 then "yA01.mif", so it is not a plain path but an encoded string stream
not_solved.mapping: the block table has 5265 entries while the name table has 3341 names, so one file can span several blocks and the mapping is not yet derived

next: decode Archive::ReadFile or whichever routine the game uses to pull a file out, since that code contains the exact inverse of this encoding.
